item.title: Mbappe Is Kicking Nike When It Is Already Down
item.description: Just when it looked like things couldn’t get any more bleak for Nike Inc., it is losing one of its biggest stars.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.title: King Charles Has an AI Summit: Britain Already Has the Best Watchdog
item.description: As the monarch convenes a meeting on the technology, humanity’s best hope for security grows in London.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: The O-Ring Risk to the Global Economy
item.description: Waking up to the threat of the weakest link causing one disaster after another.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: AI Panic Takes a Page From Medieval Millenarianism
item.description: The Mainstream Media has finally caught up with The Watchtower, the Jehovah’s Witnesses signature publication, and turned the spotlight on the end of the world. item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Hollywood Got Too Comfortable With Ryan Murphy’s Monsters
item.description: Despite Ryan Murphy’s success as a writer, producer and director, there has always been sharp criticism of his style of mashing up sex and violence into an unsavory stew. Naysayers lament the corrosiveness of such content, referencing years of social science regarding the potentially numbing effects on those who marinate in grisly fare.
item.dc:creator: Brian Lowry

item.title: Interest Rate Hike: Warsh Did Well. Where Does the Fed Go Now?
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh had ground to make up on Wednesday — and, for the most part, did what was necessary.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Noncitizens Don’t Sway Elections, Even in a Pro-Trump Tally
item.description: Last month, the Census Bureau published a strange little document claiming that “over 24,000” votes were cast by noncitizens in the 2020 US general election. The anonymous report has come under fire for its provenance and methods: It was reportedly produced outside of regular Census Bureau channels by political appointees and staffers at a think tank with close ties to President Donald Trump, using an approach that, according to one former high-level bureau official, was likely to turn up far mo
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: Bessent Got Ahead of Himself on Japan
item.description: It was always going to be a stretch for Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda to sound very hawkish. Given that officials have tightened cautiously the past two years, something major would have to change to hike interest rates at a faster pace.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss and Gearoid Reidy

item.title: The US Wants China to Know It Has Weapons in Space
item.description: In a surprising statement this week, Secretary of the Air Force Troy E. Meink revealed that the US has weapons in space. He said, “We are increasing readiness against existing threats, and the United States has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action.”
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: Diesel Is Coming for Trucking, Your Home — and the Midterms
item.description: US energy politics usually begin and end with gasoline prices. Those are at a seasonal record, but even $4.44 a gallon pales against diesel, now at an all-time high of $6.40. Most drivers’ eyes skim over that bit of the price sign — it’s called a gas station, after all — but America can’t afford to look away. Diesel isn’t just an immediate price (and politics) problem; it’s building up vulnerabilities for the US on several fronts that will play out through winter and into 2027.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: AI Panic Needs Some Nuclear Metaphors
item.description: Much about the global AI panic — could it really “kill us all by the end of the decade”? — is genuinely new, and thus extra-scary. Then again, the specter of human-engineered extinction is hardly novel; we have about eight decades of experience in thinking about it.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: King Charles Has a Perfect AI Watchdog for OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: King Charles met with executives from the world’s top artificial intelligence companies this week, just as they were calling for government help in regulating their risky, frontier systems. The king should point to a source of help in his own backyard.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: When War Damages Cultural Treasures, What Can UNESCO Do?
item.description: I don’t know if artificial intelligence poses an existential threat, but the human damage to civilization’s cultural legacy is a matter of record. It continues to this day with the violent erosion of our historical heritage through war.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan
